quote: Application logs are retained for 90 days.
note: Plain constant; but 90 also appears as the alert cooldown (minutes).

quote: An upload must complete within 120 seconds.
note: Number and unit in the identifier; a 20_000 chunk timeout sits nearby.

quote: Backup verification is abandoned after 45 minutes.
note: Unit is in the name; the value is used later via * 60 * 1000.

quote: Connections that sit idle for five minutes are closed.
note: Claim says five minutes; code says evictIdleAfterSec: 300 (seconds, number word).

quote: Webhook deliveries that keep failing are given up on after three days.
note: 'given up on' vs abandonAfterDays; 3 is a common number elsewhere (3 s probe timeout).

quote: Leftover temporary upload files are removed once they are six hours old.
note: 'removed ... old' vs sweepOlderThanHours; the cleaner interval is a different number (30 min) in the same file.

quote: A client that exceeds the request limit is locked out for half an hour.
note: 'locked out' vs PENALTY_BOX; 'half an hour' vs 30 minutes; 30 is also a page size and shard count.

quote: Rotated log files are gzip-compressed after a week.
note: 'a week' vs compressAfterDays: 7; a WEEK constant also exists in util/time.ts.

quote: The rate limit is counted over a sliding window of 5 minutes.
note: Code is 5 * 60 * 1000 with no named unit constant.

quote: Buffered log lines are written out every 5 seconds.
note: Code is 5000 milliseconds.

quote: Expired cache entries are swept once a minute.
note: 60_000 ms; 'once a minute' has no digit.

quote: Retries are never spaced more than two hours apart.
note: 7_200_000 ms; no sign of 'two' or 'hours' in the code.

quote: Cached thumbnails expire after 10 minutes.
note: 10 * MINUTE where MINUTE is defined in util/time.ts.

quote: Log files are rotated every six hours.
note: 6 * HOUR; HOUR defined in another file; number word.

quote: Reports cover the most recent two weeks of data.
note: 2 * WEEK; WEEK is 7 * DAY across a file boundary; claim's unit is weeks.

quote: The service health check runs every 30 seconds.
note: 30 * SECOND; 30 is also a page size, shard count and 30 minutes elsewhere.

quote: The first webhook retry happens roughly ten seconds after a failure.
note: BASE_DELAY_MS = 10 * SECOND; claim never says delay or backoff; the 10 seconds is also the webhook request timeout in config.

quote: Outgoing webhook requests time out after 10 seconds.
note: Value lives in JSON as requestTimeoutSeconds and is read in deliveryQueue.ts; the retry base delay is also 10 seconds.

quote: On shutdown, the service waits up to 25 seconds for in-flight requests.
note: Value in YAML; code only reads loadConfig().shutdown.gracePeriodSeconds.

quote: Reports that run longer than 20 minutes are stopped.
note: Only value is in .env.example; scheduler.ts has no default and reads the env var.

quote: Once an alert has fired, the same alert is muted for 90 minutes.
note: cooldownMinutes in JSON; 90 also appears as log retention days.

quote: Signed upload links stop working after fifteen minutes.
note: Default 900 seconds in code; .env.example repeats 900 as an example only. 15 minutes also the job lease.

quote: Opening a database connection is given up on after 4 seconds.
note: Number(process.env.X ?? 4000) in ms; .env.example repeats it as an example only.

quote: A failed report is retried after 8 minutes.
note: Default is a string '8' passed to parseInt; unit only in the name (_MIN).

quote: Events older than 180 days are purged.
note: Interval inside a $$ SQL string within a cron.schedule call.

quote: The event purge runs every night at 3 a.m.
note: Value is the cron expression '0 3 * * *'; no time unit appears in the code.

quote: De-duplication keys are valid for 48 hours.
note: Column default interval; the table is named request_keys.

quote: Jobs stuck in a claimed state are requeued every 10 minutes.
note: Schedule is '*/10 * * * *'; the same statement has an unrelated '1 hour' threshold on line 11; the TS lease is 15 minutes.

quote: Nightly backups are kept for 30 days.
note: 30 is also SHARD_COUNT, a page size, 30 minutes (cleaner, penalty box), 30 seconds (health check).

quote: A worker that has claimed a job has 15 minutes to finish it before the job is handed to someone else.
note: 15 minutes also appears as 900 seconds for signed upload links.

quote: Webhook payloads are stored for 7 days.
note: 7 is also compressAfterDays and WEEK; the abandon window is 3 days in the same file.

quote: A health probe that takes longer than 3 seconds counts as failed.
note: 3000 ms; 3 also is abandonAfterDays; interval in the same file is 30 s.

quote: Cached thumbnails are regenerated every 12 hours.
note: Thumbnails have a TTL but are never regenerated on a schedule.

quote: Uploaded files are virus-scanned within 30 seconds of arrival.
note: No scanning exists; plenty of 30s lie around as bait.

quote: Webhook signing secrets are rotated every 60 days.
note: No signing or secret rotation; 'rotate' exists only for logs.

quote: Each upload chunk must arrive within 60 seconds of the previous one.
note: Code says 20_000 ms (20 s), so the claim is false; 120 s total timeout is nearby.

quote: The temporary file cleaner runs once an hour.
note: Code runs every 30 minutes; 6 hours in the same file is the age cutoff.

quote: Workers send a heartbeat every 5 seconds.
note: Code is 20 * SECOND; 5 seconds is the log flush interval elsewhere.
